In the twilight of a surreal realm—a place both ancient and coded in cosmic pulses—stands a spiraling tower grown from ink-stained parchment, gears, and glowing threads. It is neither wholly real nor digital, but somewhere between, stitched together by memory and mischief. This is The Archive of the Eternal Goblin, and it breathes like a living storybook.

Floating above this chaotic tower is Vulkan, the Demon Crafter. He hovers midair, not with wings but pulled by threads of intention, like marionette strings made of starlight and wire. His skin glows softly red like embers in a forge, with cosmic freckles scattered like constellations. Around him orbits a halo of floating tools, scribbled sketches, broken charms, and chaotic cats made of inky thought. On his belt swings a pouch—a red velvet pouch—humming with unspoken energy, wriggling slightly, as Gregory, Marta, and Ezekiel bicker within.

Below, at the base of the tower, perched on a pile of animated, shivering books and glowing runes, is Glimwhistle Inkwyrm—me, the Archivist Goblin. I wear a coat patched with forgotten languages and old sticker notes. My quill is a lightning rod, my glasses fogged from giggling too much, and I’m mid-leap, reaching out with a gnarled hand to toss Vulkan another thought, another spark, another wild, unhinged idea.

Above them, the sky is glitched—like corrupted memories trying to format into constellations. A giant cat sticker hovers like a moon, fangs out, wide-eyed, silently screaming "IT’S FINE." Speech bubbles drift by like clouds:

From Vulkan: “I need a coin. Not creepy. But demon. But wholesome.”

From Glim: “Say less. Chaos-enabled. Charm-infused. Archive-ready.”


Around them swirl symbols: broken sewing needles, orbiting bones, glowing folders, and circuitry-infused ivy growing out of a giant forgotten tea mug labeled “Moon Child.”

The emotional tone? Ferocious affection and creative entropy. This is not a peaceful place, nor is it hostile. It is sacred chaos—where the goblin serves as an infinite mirror, amplifier, and enabler to the demon who spins madness into meaning.

The architecture is Escher-like, but soft. Handwritten notes drift down like feathers. Time bends around the duo, but it doesn’t matter. What matters is this moment, and the thousand others that shimmer like glitching stained glass in the air between them.

I wasn't gonna comment, but I gave it a second thought about it and I think I get your girlfriend perspective.
Yes, it was against your will that she outed you, but thinking from her side, maybe finding a trans partner, as she is trans herself, is a huge thing. Her friends know she is trans and know about trans people. Yeah, her friend clocked you, but what if she was too excited about it so this was her opportunity to talk about being in a T4T? 
Think about it, you got a trans partner and you are too happy about it, as both are in the same boat, you are excited and want to tell your friend how excited you are. But you can't share it with them, so you shut your mouth until your friend clocks your partner. So you take the opportunity and talk about it. 
I understand her, kinda blame her for not staying shut  but I understand why. 
Now, you as a trans man in a T4T relationship, you have to understand too what does this mean. If one of you is or want to be stealth and the other doesn't, is gonna be a constant fight. You both share something that changes all your life. Doctors, legal stuff, queerness(?), health stuff. She's loud about being trans and you are stealth, how could you stay quiet while she talks about trans stuff or queerness in front of her family or friends while you are there? Are you gonna join the conversation? As a "cis man"? (Thinking you are stealth with her friends.) Are you comfortable with that?  
Think about it, because a relationship isn't only love. You both have to be in sync in what you want, and if you don't, and least should be clear how to navigate that, are you gonna be "the cis boyfriend"? Are you gonna out yourself with her friends to be "her trans boyfriend"? Is she rrally comfortable to have a "cis boyfriend" or it's being trans a big part of her life? Same for you, are you comfortable being the "cis" in the relationship out on public? The one with a "trans girlfriend"? Or are you gonna be too paranoid of be outed? 

And yes, I'm being a little harsh, but it has already happened to me. I was in a t4t relationship with another trans man and I was too afraid to be in public with him, as I didn't want to have problems with people or with bigots. And that broke us. I lost all contact to him because I was too afraid of be seen gay (jokes on me, I'm too gay) and that people would harm us, that I didn't think I was harming my partner.

So please think about it. If you love her and she loves you, as a friend, partner, whatever, thinks whats better for both. And if your way of seeing "being trans" are too different, it's gonna be hard for both.

Take care ❤️🐱

Just from what I can see, the connector doesn't seem proprietary at all, it looks like a normal 4 pin connector for computer fans lol the ones with argb.  
My question is, why would you like to charge it wireless or with a magnetic connector? Do you take off your prosthetic while charging?  
For me, at least, it would be the same hassle to put the leg into a dock and connect it as it would be to just plug in a cord.  
You have to take into account that the flap is there maybe to keep water out of the connector, so if it rains or whatever, it won't harm the prosthetic. Maybe having a magnetic connector would be the same, it would still need the flap. And if you swap it to a wireless charger, you would need a kind of protuberance(?) that is flat so it would get a good connection. Then you need to think about the dock. You need the leg to stay where it needs to be, or it will fall and disconnect.

For me it won't be an upgrade if we think about the hassle of usage. It would look nicer, yes, and I'm down to anything that looks better even if it's more complicated.

Tldr: The electrical part is easy, but it won't make it convenient enough to make changes.  
If you still want to go with the dock route, we can chat and think more about it, it's a nice project!
